name: Name three-dimensional objects
description: Student can name familiar three-dimensional objects such as cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, prism and pyramid.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown a cylinder, the student names it.
commonError: Student names a 3D object by a related 2D shape, calling a cube a square.
checkpointTask: Show 3D objects. Ask the student to name each.

name: Describe key features of an object
description: Student can describe a 3D object by features such as its faces, edges and vertices, or curved and flat surfaces.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a cube has 6 flat square faces and 8 corners.
commonError: Student counts faces or corners incorrectly, or describes only the look.
checkpointTask: Show 3D objects. Ask the student to describe the features of each.

name: Classify objects by features
description: Student can classify a collection of 3D objects by key features.
exampleOfSuccess: The student sorts objects into those that roll and those that do not.
commonError: Student sorts by colour or size rather than a geometric feature.
checkpointTask: Give a set of 3D objects. Ask the student to sort them by a feature and explain the rule.

name: Make a three-dimensional object
description: Student can make a 3D object using materials such as connecting cubes or straws.
exampleOfSuccess: The student builds a rectangular prism from connecting cubes.
commonError: Student builds an object that does not match the named one.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to make a named 3D object with materials.

name: Explain why a feature suits a use
description: Student can explain why an object's features make it suited to its use.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a cylinder rolls, so it suits a can that needs to roll off a shelf, or a ball is a sphere so it rolls in any direction.
commonError: Student describes the object but not why its features suit the use.
checkpointTask: Show objects with a use. Ask the student why the shape suits the job.

name: Locate landmarks on a map
description: Student can locate key landmarks on a simple two-dimensional map.
exampleOfSuccess: On a map of the classroom, the student finds the door and the reading corner.
commonError: Student cannot match map symbols to real places.
checkpointTask: Give a simple map. Ask the student to find named landmarks.

name: Describe positions relative to each other
description: Student can describe where landmarks are in relation to each other on a map.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the library is next to the office and across from the hall.
commonError: Student describes places in isolation rather than in relation to each other.
checkpointTask: Show a map. Ask the student to describe where places are relative to one another.

name: Create a map of a familiar space
description: Student can create a two-dimensional map of a familiar space showing key features.
exampleOfSuccess: The student sketches the classroom showing the door, desks and reading corner in roughly the right places.
commonError: Student draws features in the wrong relative positions, or leaves out key ones.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to draw a map of a familiar space showing its key features.

name: Use a plan to locate yourself
description: Student can use a simple hand-held plan to locate themselves within a space.
exampleOfSuccess: Holding a plan, the student points to where they are standing.
commonError: Student cannot relate their real position to the plan.
checkpointTask: Give the student a plan of the room. Ask them to show where they are.

name: Mark a route or location on a map
description: Student can mark a route or a hidden location on a map and explain it.
exampleOfSuccess: The student marks where an object is hidden and describes the path to it.
commonError: Student marks a location inconsistent with the real space.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to mark a location or route on a map and describe it.
